## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：lit-nte-1。

### 候选资料：lit-nte-1（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaClO4；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：TEP, EMC；溶剂比例（体积）：TEP=0.8, EMC=0.2；添加剂：VC；添加剂用量：VC=3 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec4::child2]：These properties make linear carbonates an ideal cosolvent for optimizing phosphate-based electrolytes and achieving synergistic performance enhancement. PB||HC full cells with EMC cosolvent exhibit better electrochemical performance than their counterparts, such as DEC, DMC, ethylene carbonate (EC), and PC in Fig. S1. And hence, the electrolyte formulation of $1.0\mathrm{MNaClO_4}$ -TEP/EMC (8:2 vol%) +3 wt% VC is designed and denoted as NTE electrolyte. The baseline electrolyte,

1.0 M NaClO $_{4}$ -TEP + 3 wt% VC, is referred to as the NT electrolyte. The incorporation of EMC preserves the inherent non-flammability of the TEP-based electrolyte without compromising its safety, while simultaneously reducing viscosity, enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability with Al foil (Fig. 1d–f, Table S2 and Video S1).

## 候选评估
### same-paper-1
评估建议：该候选在无氟性、目标全电池构型及约 50 °C（原文 55 °C 实测）循环上均有直接原文支持，但作为选择条件的“低成本”仅有一般性动机、缺乏候选自身依据，且高倍率性能明显受限，故当前证据不足以给出推荐，暂持 hold，待补充 NaBOB/TEP/PES 的成本或原料可得性直接证据后再决。
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- 候选电解质配方身份：0.35 M NaBOB 溶于 TEP，并含 3 wt% PES 添加剂：原文多处将该配方写作 0.35 M NaBOB–TEP + 3 wt% PES，并说明其为本文研究对象，与候选的盐/溶剂/添加剂及浓度一致。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec4::child1][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec12::child0][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec8::child0]
- 无氟（fluorine-free）电解液：原文明确把 NaBOB–TEP + 3 wt% PES 称为 non-flammable and fluorine-free electrolyte，且其盐与溶剂均不含氟（对照为含 NaPF6 的碳酸酯电解液）。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec8::child3][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec1::child0]
- 目标电芯构型：hard carbon || Prussian white 钠离子全电池：原文在 Fig. 6 说明与实验部分均写明使用 Prussian white–hard carbon 全电池，并给出 Prussian white（12 mg cm^-2）与 hard carbon（7 mg cm^-2）、N/P=1.1 的电极信息。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec4::child1][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec11::child0]
- 运行温度约 50 °C：把“around 50 C”按温度读（全部来源均为温度—性能研究且电芯构型一致）；原文在 40 °C 与 55 °C 实测，55 °C 下 0.2 C 稳定循环并达到与 NaPF6/EC:DEC 相当的容量保持，覆盖“约 50 °C”。若把 50 C 读作倍率，则 sec5 显示该候选在 2 C 已严重衰减，属反证；本评估采用温度读法。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec8::child0][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec4::child1][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec5]
- 低成本（候选本身或其组成的直接成本依据）：原文只有 SIB 相对 LIB 可能更低成本的一般性动机表述，未对 NaBOB/TEP/PES 该候选给出成本、原料丰度或与替代电解液的直接成本对比，因此不能据此判定该候选满足低成本选择条件。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec1::child0]
文献与候选的关联：来源为该论文自身实验：其用 0.35 M NaBOB–TEP + 3 wt% PES 电解液装配 Prussian white||hard carbon 全电池，并在 55 °C（另有 40 °C）进行恒流循环与倍率测试，因此配方—电芯构型—温度条件之间的关联由同一实验描述直接建立；但该实验未给出该候选的成本数据，且其倍率测试显示在 2 C 已显著容量衰减。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec11::child0][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec4::child1][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec5]
### same-paper-2
评估建议：The candidate is supported for the low-cost, fluorine-free, hard-carbon||Prussian-white full-cell requirements, but the critical around-50 C rate requirement is unsupported by the provided sources and no computations were recorded, so a recommendation is withheld pending rate-capability evidence.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Fluorine-free electrolyte：The paper explicitly describes NaBOB dissolved in TMP as a nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte, and the salt contains no fluorine. [0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec4::child0][0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec1::child1]
- Low-cost electrolyte：The paper states the lower 0.5 M NaBOB concentration versus conventional 1 M NaPF6 reduces electrolyte cost and that NaBOB raw materials are common and benign. [0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec3::child1]
- Hard-carbon||Prussian-white sodium-ion full cell：The electrolyte was evaluated in two-electrode sodium-ion full cells consisting of a hard carbon anode and a Prussian white cathode. [0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec3::child3][0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec1::child1]
- 0.5 M NaBOB in TMP composition matches candidate：The paper repeatedly uses 0.5 M NaBOB in TMP, the maximum clear concentration in TMP, matching the candidate's salt and concentration. [0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec3::child1][0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec4::child0]
- Operation around 50 C (high-rate capability)：The reported full-cell galvanostatic cycling is at 30 mA g^-1 (low rate); the sources provide no high-rate or 50 C performance for this candidate, and no rate computation was recorded. 
文献与候选的关联：The candidate's 0.5 M NaBOB in TMP was tested directly in two-electrode hard-carbon||Prussian-white pouch full cells cycled between 1 and 3.8 V at 30 mA g^-1, so the HC||PW full-cell and cost/fluorine-free claims are directly linked to this candidate; however these tests are low-rate and establish no 50 C behavior. [0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec3::child3][0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec5::child3][0245_acsaem0c00522pdf::sec5::child2]
### lit-nte-1
评估建议：The literature directly supports every extracted requirement for this candidate: it is fluorine-free, presented as cost-effective, defined by the exact NTE composition, and demonstrated in PB||HC full cells over a temperature window spanning ~50 °C. With no recorded computations contradicting this, the evidence supports recommending lit-nte-1.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Fluorine-free electrolyte (no fluorinated salt/solvent/additive)：The abstract explicitly describes an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate–phosphate mixed solvent system, and the conclusion repeats 'fluorine-free'; the listed components (NaClO4, TEP, EMC, VC) contain no fluorine. [0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0][0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec3::child2]
- Applicable to a hard-carbon||Prussian-white (PB||HC) sodium-ion full cell：The full-cell section reports PB||HC full cells with the NTE electrolyte (including high-mass-loading electrodes), and the abstract/conclusion state the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell shows stable cycling, matching the target chemistry. [0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec8::child0][0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec9::child0]
- Operation around 50 °C：Interpreting '50 C' as temperature (consistent with this high-temperature paper), PB||HC cells with NTE operate stably over 10–100 °C, with detailed cycling at 55 °C and cylindrical-cell data at 55 °C (and 80 °C); 50 °C lies within the demonstrated window. source_refs.raw_quote: The thermal stability of NaBOB-TEP electrolytes with PES or DTD additives as well as a reference carbonate electrolyte based on $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ in EC:DEC was studied through storage at elevated temperature of $55^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . NMR spectroscopy results revealed partial degradation of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ likely forming difluorophosphoric acid $(\mathrm{O} = \mathrm{PF}_2(\mathrm{OH})$ , and full degradation of DTD in a transesterification reaction with TEP solvent forming diethyl sulfate and ethyl ethylene phosphate. The degradation of DTD in the NaBOB-TEP electrolyte solution starts already at room temperature, discoloring the electrolyte. However, NaBOB-TEP electrolyte with and without PES additive remained stable after 4 weeks storage at $55^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The electrochemical performance of Prussian white–hard carbon full-cells was investigated at $40\ °C$ and $55\ °C$ under different cycling protocols, including galvanostatic cycling with and without extended relaxation time and different cycling rates. 0.35 M NaBOB in TEP with 3 wt% PES electrolyte solution showed promising results, obtaining stable cycling at 55 °C at 0.2 C rate and reaching comparable capacity retention after 140 cycles as 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in EC:DEC at the same condition. The NaFP $_{6}$ electrolyte on the other hand experienced an acceleration in capacity fade after around 100 cycles.

source_refs.raw_quote:
Jonas Welch, Wessel W. A. van Ekeren, Jonas Mindemark & Reza Younesi

Check for updates

Sodium-ion batteries are a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries due to their potential for lower cost and greater sustainability. However, achieving stable cycling performance, particularly at high mass-loadings and elevated temperatures, remains a challenge. The stable cycling of high mass-loading sodium-ion battery cells is here made possible by addition of prop-1-ene-1,3-sultone (PES) to a non-flammable and fluorine-free electrolyte solution of sodium bis(oxalato)borate (NaBOB) salt in triethyl phosphate (TEP). This study investigates the thermal stability and electrochemical performance of such electrolyte at 40 °C and 55 °C, contrasting their performance with base NaBOB in TEP with and without ethylene sulfate (DTD) additive and with a reference carbonate electrolyte of $NaPF_{6}$ in ethylene carbonate:diethylene carbonate (EC:DEC). Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy was used to reveal degradation products formed in the electrolyte following a 4-weeks storage at 55 °C. Results from galvanostatic cycling at 55 °C demonstrated comparable performance of NaBOB–TEP + PES electrolyte and the reference carbonate electrolyte. The internal cell resistance was initially lower when cells were cycled at 55 °C than at 40 °C for all studied electrolytes.

The results in Fig. 6 show that the cell with carbonate-based electrolyte outperformed the cell with 0.35 M NaBOB-TEP + PES at high C-rates as the latter suffered from major capacity fading at 2 C. source_refs.raw_quote: This finding enables a nonflammable electrolyte with high ionic conductivity and promising electrochemical performance in full-cell sodium-ion batteries. An electrolyte of 0.5 M NaBOB in TMP provides an ionic conductivity of 5 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is comparable to the commonly used electrolytes based on sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_{6}$ ) and organic carbonate solvents. The proposed electrolyte shows a Coulombic efficiency of above 80% in the first cycle, which increased to about 97% from the second cycle in sodium-ion battery full-cells consisting of a hard carbon anode and a Prussian white cathode. This work opens up opportunities to design safe electrolytes which can further be optimized with electrolyte additives such as vinylene carbonate for industrial applications. KEYWORDS: electrolyte salt, non-flammable, fire-retardant, hardcarbon, full-cell, Na-ion battery, TMP, NaBOB

"Structure, Conductivity, and Flammability". The synthesis and structural properties of NaBOB has previously been investigated by Zavalij et al., $^{19}$ and their work provided a good foundation for the synthesis and determination of the purity of the NaBOB. LiBOB performance is sensitive to impurities, $^{17}$ and therefore, NaBOB was recrystallized in TMP in our work. Figure 1 shows X-ray diffraction, elemental analysis, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) of NaBOB salt synthesized in this work. The combined results from X-ray diffraction (XRD) and elemental analysis based on combustion analysis and inductively coupled plasma (ICP)—optical emission spectroscopy (OES) show that the salt has high purity as proven by the stoichiometry. No impurity phase was detected in the diffractogram (see Tables S1 supplemental for XRD analysis details). The TGA results indicate that NaBOB salt is stable up to 300 °C in nitrogen, which is an important advantage compared to $NaPF_{6}$ being stable up to 140 °C under vacuum. $^{30}$

Figure 2 shows that the ionic conductivity of NaBOB–TMP increases with NaBOB concentration, ultimately reaching 5 mS cm $^{-1}$ for 0.5 M NaBOB in the TMP electrolyte at room temperature, which is similar to the corresponding ionic conductivity of 6 mS cm $^{-1}$ for 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in TMP.

The 0.5 M NaBOB in the TMP electrolyte was further evaluated in two-electrode sodium-ion full cells consisting of a hard carbon anode and a Prussian white cathode. The results in Figure 5a,b show that the NaBOB-TMP electrolyte provides superior cycling performance compared to the $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ -TMP electrolyte with Coulombic efficiency (CE) at $75\%$ compared to that of $55\%$ for $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ for the first cycle. The additive-free NaBOB-TMP electrolyte enables stable cycling while the additive-free $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ -TMP, in accordance with the literature,[33] has very poor performance and only maintains 31 mAh $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ at the 10th cycle compared to the $108\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{h}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ of NaBOB-TMP. The SEI formation in the NaBOB-based electrolyte was observed between 1.5 and $2.5\mathrm{V}$ during the first charge, and the early NaBOB decomposition into carbonates stabilize the TMP solvent while $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ clearly suffers from suboptimal passivation. Figure 5c,d displays the voltage profile of hard carbon anode and the Prussian white cathode individually versus the reference electrode in a three-electrode cell.

Results from the best performing cells of all replicates, showing specific discharge capacity based on the cathode mass (a) and CE for the same cells (b). NaBOB in TMP enables relatively high CE in hard carbon-based full-cell sodium-ion cells. The proposed electrolyte can of course be further optimized using electrolyte additives to achieve higher initial CEs and an improved cycle life. As one example, VC has here been shown to improve the electrochemical performance of full-cell sodium batteries using the studied electrolyte compositions. Overall, this means that high energy-density cells ( $>250\ W\ h\ kg^{-1}$ based on active materials) built from low-cost and abundant materials can be cycled at Columbic efficiencies above 99%. This is in cells with electrolytes that cannot burn using a solvent that freezes at a low $-46\ ^{\circ}C$ , without the environmental and health aspects of using highly fluorinated compounds. In short, this work is a promising step to remove most of the problems that state-of-the-art electrolytes suffer from.

These properties make linear carbonates an ideal cosolvent for optimizing phosphate-based electrolytes and achieving synergistic performance enhancement. PB||HC full cells with EMC cosolvent exhibit better electrochemical performance than their counterparts, such as DEC, DMC, ethylene carbonate (EC), and PC in Fig. S1. And hence, the electrolyte formulation of $1.0\mathrm{MNaClO_4}$ -TEP/EMC (8:2 vol%) +3 wt% VC is designed and denoted as NTE electrolyte. The baseline electrolyte,

1.0 M NaClO $_{4}$ -TEP + 3 wt% VC, is referred to as the NT electrolyte. The incorporation of EMC preserves the inherent non-flammability of the TEP-based electrolyte without compromising its safety, while simultaneously reducing viscosity, enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability with Al foil (Fig. 1d–f, Table S2 and Video S1).

source_refs.raw_quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

source_refs.raw_quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

source_refs.raw_quote: As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%. Besides, NTE-based cylindrical cell also demonstrates superior rate capacity at 55 °C in Figs. 5f and S20. Furthermore, the NTE electrolyte maintains robust cyclability in cylindrical cells even at 80 °C, retaining 89.7% of its initial capacity after 50 cycles (Fig. S21). The universality of NTE electrolyte is further validated in full cells incorporating a layered oxide (NFM) cathode. The NTE-based cells consistently exhibit enhanced long-term cycling stability and rate performance at both 25 °C and 55 °C, as substantiated in Fig. 5g, h and S22-S26. These collective findings confirm the universal applicability and superior high-temperature stability of the designed NTE electrolyte.

A rate-test was performed for the $NaPF_{6}$ -EC:DEC and NaBOB-TEP + PES electrolytes at 55 °C, as the higher temperature enables higher ionic conductivity and potentially lower overall resistance. The results in Fig. 6 show that the cell with carbonate-based electrolyte outperformed the cell with 0.35 M NaBOB-TEP + PES at high C-rates as the latter suffered from major capacity fading at 2 C. The cause of this could be a result of the relatively lower ionic conductivity of NaBOB-TEP electrolyte, resulting in mostly active material close to the macro surface of the electrodes contributing with sodium ions. Alternatively, it could stem from a high-impedance SEI layer, as evidenced by the nearly doubled cell resistance measured via ICI (see Fig. 5).

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, this work successfully developed an intrinsically nonflammable, fluorine-free, and high-temperature compatible electrolyte through solvation structure engineering. By introducing weakly coordinating EMC into a phosphate-based system, greater incorporation of anions and additives into the inner $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath is constructed. This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

source_refs.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec3::child2
source_refs.paper_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt
source_refs.raw_quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

source_refs.raw_quote: To further evaluate the practical relevance of NTE electrolyte, PB|| HC full cells with high-mass loading electrodes are assembled (Fig. 4a). Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). As shown in Figs. 4d and S12, the NTE electrolyte enables markedly enhanced rate performance. The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. This advantage is maintained at a high rate of $1.5\mathrm{C}$ , where the NTE-based cell retains $69.2\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , in contrast to only $42.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ for the NT-based cell. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is employed to evaluate the interfacial stability of PB||HC cells with different electrolytes in Figs. 4f, S13 and Table S8.

citations.quote: The thermal stability of NaBOB-TEP electrolytes with PES or DTD additives as well as a reference carbonate electrolyte based on $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ in EC:DEC was studied through storage at elevated temperature of $55^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The degradation of DTD in the NaBOB-TEP electrolyte solution starts already at room temperature, discoloring the electrolyte. citations.quote:
Jonas Welch, Wessel W. A. van Ekeren, Jonas Mindemark & Reza Younesi

Check for updates

Sodium-ion batteries are a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries due to their potential for lower cost and greater sustainability. However, achieving stable cycling performance, particularly at high mass-loadings and elevated temperatures, remains a challenge. The stable cycling of high mass-loading sodium-ion battery cells is here made possible by addition of prop-1-ene-1,3-sultone (PES) to a non-flammable and fluorine-free electrolyte solution of sodium bis(oxalato)borate (NaBOB) salt in triethyl phosphate (TEP). This study investigates the thermal stability and electrochemical performance of such electrolyte at 40 °C and 55 °C, contrasting their performance with base NaBOB in TEP with and without ethylene sulfate (DTD) additive and with a reference carbonate electrolyte of $NaPF_{6}$ in ethylene carbonate:diethylene carbonate (EC:DEC). Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy was used to reveal degradation products formed in the electrolyte following a 4-weeks storage at 55 °C. Results from galvanostatic cycling at 55 °C demonstrated comparable performance of NaBOB–TEP + PES electrolyte and the reference carbonate electrolyte. The internal cell resistance was initially lower when cells were cycled at 55 °C than at 40 °C for all studied electrolytes.

Electrode disks were cut from foil sheets to 20 mm in diameter, before dried for 15 h in a vacuum oven at 170 °C, after which they were kept in an argon-filled glovebox. Pouch cells were assembled in the glovebox with 150 $\mu$ L electrolyte, Dreamweaver gold separator, and 5 mm wide current collector tabs cut from thicker Al foil and placed behind each electrode disc. Galvanostatic cycling and Intermittent current interruption (ICI)

Full cells were cycled at $40\ °C$ or $55\ °C$ in a Novonix High Precision Charger System or Arbin Instruments battery testing system. The internal resistance of some cells was studied with ICI, for which an Arbin Instruments battery testing system was used. Some of the cells were equipped with reference electrodes based on preconditioned Prussian white, as in the previous publication $^{36}$ . Every 5 min, a 1 s pause with a recorded datapoint every 0.1 s was initiated. As the pause is initiated, there is a voltage drop linearly proportional to $t^{\frac{1}{2}}$ .

Jonas Welch, Wessel W. A. van Ekeren, Jonas Mindemark & Reza Younesi

Check for updates

Sodium-ion batteries are a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries due to their potential for lower cost and greater sustainability. However, achieving stable cycling performance, particularly at high mass-loadings and elevated temperatures, remains a challenge. The stable cycling of high mass-loading sodium-ion battery cells is here made possible by addition of prop-1-ene-1,3-sultone (PES) to a non-flammable and fluorine-free electrolyte solution of sodium bis(oxalato)borate (NaBOB) salt in triethyl phosphate (TEP). This study investigates the thermal stability and electrochemical performance of such electrolyte at 40 °C and 55 °C, contrasting their performance with base NaBOB in TEP with and without ethylene sulfate (DTD) additive and with a reference carbonate electrolyte of $NaPF_{6}$ in ethylene carbonate:diethylene carbonate (EC:DEC). Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy was used to reveal degradation products formed in the electrolyte following a 4-weeks storage at 55 °C. Results from galvanostatic cycling at 55 °C demonstrated comparable performance of NaBOB–TEP + PES electrolyte and the reference carbonate electrolyte. The internal cell resistance was initially lower when cells were cycled at 55 °C than at 40 °C for all studied electrolytes.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.quote: In summary, this work successfully developed an intrinsically nonflammable, fluorine-free, and high-temperature compatible electrolyte through solvation structure engineering. By introducing weakly coordinating EMC into a phosphate-based system, greater incorporation of anions and additives into the inner $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath is constructed. This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

citations.quote: In summary, this work successfully developed an intrinsically nonflammable, fluorine-free, and high-temperature compatible electrolyte through solvation structure engineering. By introducing weakly coordinating EMC into a phosphate-based system, greater incorporation of anions and additives into the inner $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath is constructed. This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

association_citations.quote: To further evaluate the practical relevance of NTE electrolyte, PB|| HC full cells with high-mass loading electrodes are assembled (Fig. 4a). Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is employed to evaluate the interfacial stability of PB||HC cells with different electrolytes in Figs. 4f, S13 and Table S8.

NMR spectroscopy results revealed partial degradation of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ likely forming difluorophosphoric acid $(\mathrm{O} = \mathrm{PF}_2(\mathrm{OH})$ , and full degradation of DTD in a transesterification reaction with TEP solvent forming diethyl sulfate and ethyl ethylene phosphate. The degradation of DTD in the NaBOB-TEP electrolyte solution starts already at room temperature, discoloring the electrolyte. However, NaBOB-TEP electrolyte with and without PES additive remained stable after 4 weeks storage at $55^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The electrochemical performance of Prussian white–hard carbon full-cells was investigated at $40\ °C$ and $55\ °C$ under different cycling protocols, including galvanostatic cycling with and without extended relaxation time and different cycling rates. 0.35 M NaBOB in TEP with 3 wt% PES electrolyte solution showed promising results, obtaining stable cycling at 55 °C at 0.2 C rate and reaching comparable capacity retention after 140 cycles as 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in EC:DEC at the same condition. The NaFP $_{6}$ electrolyte on the other hand experienced an acceleration in capacity fade after around 100 cycles.

Sodium-ion batteries are a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries due to their potential for lower cost and greater sustainability. However, achieving stable cycling performance, particularly at high mass-loadings and elevated temperatures, remains a challenge. The stable cycling of high mass-loading sodium-ion battery cells is here made possible by addition of prop-1-ene-1,3-sultone (PES) to a non-flammable and fluorine-free electrolyte solution of sodium bis(oxalato)borate (NaBOB) salt in triethyl phosphate (TEP). This study investigates the thermal stability and electrochemical performance of such electrolyte at 40 °C and 55 °C, contrasting their performance with base NaBOB in TEP with and without ethylene sulfate (DTD) additive and with a reference carbonate electrolyte of $NaPF_{6}$ in ethylene carbonate:diethylene carbonate (EC:DEC). Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy was used to reveal degradation products formed in the electrolyte following a 4-weeks storage at 55 °C. Results from galvanostatic cycling at 55 °C demonstrated comparable performance of NaBOB–TEP + PES electrolyte and the reference carbonate electrolyte. The internal cell resistance was initially lower when cells were cycled at 55 °C than at 40 °C for all studied electrolytes.

Figure 4g, h present the cycling results of the reference cells using the carbonate electrolyte. The addition of PES and DTD to the $NaPF_{6}$ in EC:DEC electrolyte showed detrimental effect on the long-term cycling performance of these cells with carbonate-based electrolytes, see Fig. S16, and are thus not suitable as high-temperature stable electrolytes.

evidence_ledger.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

evidence_ledger.quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, this work successfully developed an intrinsically nonflammable, fluorine-free, and high-temperature compatible electrolyte through solvation structure engineering. By introducing weakly coordinating EMC into a phosphate-based system, greater incorporation of anions and additives into the inner $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath is constructed. This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

evidence_ledger.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

citations.quote: The thermal stability of NaBOB-TEP electrolytes with PES or DTD additives as well as a reference carbonate electrolyte based on $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ in EC:DEC was studied through storage at elevated temperature of $55^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . NMR spectroscopy results revealed partial degradation of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ likely forming difluorophosphoric acid $(\mathrm{O} = \mathrm{PF}_2(\mathrm{OH})$ , and full degradation of DTD in a transesterification reaction with TEP solvent forming diethyl sulfate and ethyl ethylene phosphate. The degradation of DTD in the NaBOB-TEP electrolyte solution starts already at room temperature, discoloring the electrolyte. However, NaBOB-TEP electrolyte with and without PES additive remained stable after 4 weeks storage at $55^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The electrochemical performance of Prussian white–hard carbon full-cells was investigated at $40\ °C$ and $55\ °C$ under different cycling protocols, including galvanostatic cycling with and without extended relaxation time and different cycling rates. 0.35 M NaBOB in TEP with 3 wt% PES electrolyte solution showed promising results, obtaining stable cycling at 55 °C at 0.2 C rate and reaching comparable capacity retention after 140 cycles as 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in EC:DEC at the same condition. The NaFP $_{6}$ electrolyte on the other hand experienced an acceleration in capacity fade after around 100 cycles.

citations.quote:
Jonas Welch, Wessel W. A. van Ekeren, Jonas Mindemark & Reza Younesi

Check for updates

Sodium-ion batteries are a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries due to their potential for lower cost and greater sustainability. However, achieving stable cycling performance, particularly at high mass-loadings and elevated temperatures, remains a challenge. The stable cycling of high mass-loading sodium-ion battery cells is here made possible by addition of prop-1-ene-1,3-sultone (PES) to a non-flammable and fluorine-free electrolyte solution of sodium bis(oxalato)borate (NaBOB) salt in triethyl phosphate (TEP). This study investigates the thermal stability and electrochemical performance of such electrolyte at 40 °C and 55 °C, contrasting their performance with base NaBOB in TEP with and without ethylene sulfate (DTD) additive and with a reference carbonate electrolyte of $NaPF_{6}$ in ethylene carbonate:diethylene carbonate (EC:DEC). Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy was used to reveal degradation products formed in the electrolyte following a 4-weeks storage at 55 °C. Results from galvanostatic cycling at 55 °C demonstrated comparable performance of NaBOB–TEP + PES electrolyte and the reference carbonate electrolyte. The internal cell resistance was initially lower when cells were cycled at 55 °C than at 40 °C for all studied electrolytes.

Electrodes were provided by LiFeSiZE AB $^{\circledR}$ , using commercial Prussian white powder Fennac produced by Altris AB $^{\circledR}$ (12 mg cm $^{-2}$ ) and hard carbon (7 mg cm $^{-2}$ ), with an N/P ratio of 1.1 for the full cells. More specific details regarding composition etc. are found in the earlier publication $^{36}$ . Electrode disks were cut from foil sheets to 20 mm in diameter, before dried for 15 h in a vacuum oven at 170 °C, after which they were kept in an argon-filled glovebox. Pouch cells were assembled in the glovebox with 150 $\mu$ L electrolyte, Dreamweaver gold separator, and 5 mm wide current collector tabs cut from thicker Al foil and placed behind each electrode disc. Galvanostatic cycling and Intermittent current interruption (ICI)

Full cells were cycled at $40\ °C$ or $55\ °C$ in a Novonix High Precision Charger System or Arbin Instruments battery testing system. The internal resistance of some cells was studied with ICI, for which an Arbin Instruments battery testing system was used. Some of the cells were equipped with reference electrodes based on preconditioned Prussian white, as in the previous publication $^{36}$ . Every 5 min, a 1 s pause with a recorded datapoint every 0.1 s was initiated. As the pause is initiated, there is a voltage drop linearly proportional to $t^{\frac{1}{2}}$ .

Rate capability
A rate-test was performed for the $NaPF_{6}$ -EC:DEC and NaBOB-TEP + PES electrolytes at 55 °C, as the higher temperature enables higher ionic conductivity and potentially lower overall resistance. The results in Fig. 6 show that the cell with carbonate-based electrolyte outperformed the cell with 0.35 M NaBOB-TEP + PES at high C-rates as the latter suffered from major capacity fading at 2 C. The cause of this could be a result of the relatively lower ionic conductivity of NaBOB-TEP electrolyte, resulting in mostly active material close to the macro surface of the electrodes contributing with sodium ions. Alternatively, it could stem from a high-impedance SEI layer, as evidenced by the nearly doubled cell resistance measured via ICI (see Fig. 5).

citations.quote: This finding enables a nonflammable electrolyte with high ionic conductivity and promising electrochemical performance in full-cell sodium-ion batteries. An electrolyte of 0.5 M NaBOB in TMP provides an ionic conductivity of 5 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is comparable to the commonly used electrolytes based on sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_{6}$ ) and organic carbonate solvents. The proposed electrolyte shows a Coulombic efficiency of above 80% in the first cycle, which increased to about 97% from the second cycle in sodium-ion battery full-cells consisting of a hard carbon anode and a Prussian white cathode. This work opens up opportunities to design safe electrolytes which can further be optimized with electrolyte additives such as vinylene carbonate for industrial applications. citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec9::child0
citations.quote: In summary, this work successfully developed an intrinsically nonflammable, fluorine-free, and high-temperature compatible electrolyte through solvation structure engineering. By introducing weakly coordinating EMC into a phosphate-based system, greater incorporation of anions and additives into the inner $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath is constructed. This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

citations.quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

citations.quote:
Jonas Welch, Wessel W. A. van Ekeren, Jonas Mindemark & Reza Younesi

Check for updates

Sodium-ion batteries are a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries due to their potential for lower cost and greater sustainability. However, achieving stable cycling performance, particularly at high mass-loadings and elevated temperatures, remains a challenge. The stable cycling of high mass-loading sodium-ion battery cells is here made possible by addition of prop-1-ene-1,3-sultone (PES) to a non-flammable and fluorine-free electrolyte solution of sodium bis(oxalato)borate (NaBOB) salt in triethyl phosphate (TEP). This study investigates the thermal stability and electrochemical performance of such electrolyte at 40 °C and 55 °C, contrasting their performance with base NaBOB in TEP with and without ethylene sulfate (DTD) additive and with a reference carbonate electrolyte of $NaPF_{6}$ in ethylene carbonate:diethylene carbonate (EC:DEC). Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy was used to reveal degradation products formed in the electrolyte following a 4-weeks storage at 55 °C. Results from galvanostatic cycling at 55 °C demonstrated comparable performance of NaBOB–TEP + PES electrolyte and the reference carbonate electrolyte. The internal cell resistance was initially lower when cells were cycled at 55 °C than at 40 °C for all studied electrolytes.

Rate capability
A rate-test was performed for the $NaPF_{6}$ -EC:DEC and NaBOB-TEP + PES electrolytes at 55 °C, as the higher temperature enables higher ionic conductivity and potentially lower overall resistance. The results in Fig. 6 show that the cell with carbonate-based electrolyte outperformed the cell with 0.35 M NaBOB-TEP + PES at high C-rates as the latter suffered from major capacity fading at 2 C. The cause of this could be a result of the relatively lower ionic conductivity of NaBOB-TEP electrolyte, resulting in mostly active material close to the macro surface of the electrodes contributing with sodium ions. Alternatively, it could stem from a high-impedance SEI layer, as evidenced by the nearly doubled cell resistance measured via ICI (see Fig. 5).

citations.quote: This finding enables a nonflammable electrolyte with high ionic conductivity and promising electrochemical performance in full-cell sodium-ion batteries. An electrolyte of 0.5 M NaBOB in TMP provides an ionic conductivity of 5 mS cm $^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is comparable to the commonly used electrolytes based on sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_{6}$ ) and organic carbonate solvents. The proposed electrolyte shows a Coulombic efficiency of above 80% in the first cycle, which increased to about 97% from the second cycle in sodium-ion battery full-cells consisting of a hard carbon anode and a Prussian white cathode. This work opens up opportunities to design safe electrolytes which can further be optimized with electrolyte additives such as vinylene carbonate for industrial applications. citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec9::child0
citations.quote: In summary, this work successfully developed an intrinsically nonflammable, fluorine-free, and high-temperature compatible electrolyte through solvation structure engineering. By introducing weakly coordinating EMC into a phosphate-based system, greater incorporation of anions and additives into the inner $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath is constructed. This process facilitates the formation of robust and stable EEI on both electrodes, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. The optimized electrolyte simultaneously achieves low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the PB||HC full cells demonstrate exceptional cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, the excellent performance is successfully validated in Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells, confirming its practical viability.

citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

citations.quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is employed to evaluate the interfacial stability of PB||HC cells with different electrolytes in Figs. 4f, S13 and Table S8.

## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：lit-nte-1。

### 候选资料：lit-nte-1（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaClO4；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：TEP, EMC；溶剂比例（体积）：TEP=0.8, EMC=0.2；添加剂：VC；添加剂用量：VC=3 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec4::child2]：These properties make linear carbonates an ideal cosolvent for optimizing phosphate-based electrolytes and achieving synergistic performance enhancement. PB||HC full cells with EMC cosolvent exhibit better electrochemical performance than their counterparts, such as DEC, DMC, ethylene carbonate (EC), and PC in Fig. S1. And hence, the electrolyte formulation of $1.0\mathrm{MNaClO_4}$ -TEP/EMC (8:2 vol%) +3 wt% VC is designed and denoted as NTE electrolyte. The baseline electrolyte,

1.0 M NaClO $_{4}$ -TEP + 3 wt% VC, is referred to as the NT electrolyte. The incorporation of EMC preserves the inherent non-flammability of the TEP-based electrolyte without compromising its safety, while simultaneously reducing viscosity, enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability with Al foil (Fig. 1d–f, Table S2 and Video S1).

## 候选评估
### same-paper-1
评估建议：该候选在无氟性、目标全电池构型及约 50 °C（原文 55 °C 实测）循环上均有直接原文支持，但作为选择条件的“低成本”仅有一般性动机、缺乏候选自身依据，且高倍率性能明显受限，故当前证据不足以给出推荐，暂持 hold，待补充 NaBOB/TEP/PES 的成本或原料可得性直接证据后再决。
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- 候选电解质配方身份：0.35 M NaBOB 溶于 TEP，并含 3 wt% PES 添加剂：原文多处将该配方写作 0.35 M NaBOB–TEP + 3 wt% PES，并说明其为本文研究对象，与候选的盐/溶剂/添加剂及浓度一致。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec4::child1][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec12::child0][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec8::child0]
- 无氟（fluorine-free）电解液：原文明确把 NaBOB–TEP + 3 wt% PES 称为 non-flammable and fluorine-free electrolyte，且其盐与溶剂均不含氟（对照为含 NaPF6 的碳酸酯电解液）。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec8::child3][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec1::child0]
- 目标电芯构型：hard carbon || Prussian white 钠离子全电池：原文在 Fig. 6 说明与实验部分均写明使用 Prussian white–hard carbon 全电池，并给出 Prussian white（12 mg cm^-2）与 hard carbon（7 mg cm^-2）、N/P=1.1 的电极信息。 [0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec4::child1][0228_Welch 等 - 2025 - Effect of additives on the high-temperature performance of a sodium bisoxalatoborate in trimethyl::sec11::child0]
